guard: Remote supervision and `cotal run --local` dial the recorded broker URL with the recorded TLS requirement, and the registration resolves its cluster digests against the store's key form
why: The broker is a real authenticated nats-server serving the same account over a TCP listener and a websocket listener. Cell A drives the registration the supervisor runs first, over the ws:// URL read back out of the mesh registry through the shipped superviseTarget. Handing that URL to the raw node transport fails with the refusal that names wsconnect, so the cell turns red while the suite still reaches its completion banner.

Cell B is the transport negative control for the first mutation only: the same registration over nats://. Under that mutant A goes red and B stays green, so killing A cannot be explained by the suite being unable to register at all. The third mutation is not a transport mutant and does not discriminate: the cluster artifact read runs on both paths, so it reddens B alongside the A it is named on.

Cell C re-records the same plaintext broker as TLS-required and requires the dial to demand TLS of it. A dial that hardcodes tls: false connects anyway and sends the prepare credential in the clear, which is the failure this cell exists to catch; the mutation below reintroduces exactly that.

The registration also reads back the cluster artifacts it just published. registerServiceInstance reports those digests as sha256:<hex> references while the content-addressed store is keyed by the bare hex, so the third mutation restores the unnormalized read and cell A goes red on the ws:// path for that second, independent reason.

Cell E drives the shipped `cotal run ps --local` verb over a ws:// mesh record. The verb opens its own planes on the server the registry resolved, so it is a second, independent command handed a registry URL, and the raw node transport refuses a websocket one there with the same wsconnect message. The cell asserts the exact line the verb prints for an empty space, so a refusal, a usage error, and a silent no-op are all red.

The trust cells (F/G/H) run the SHIPPED `cotal supervise` child against a full user-auth host rig (dev IdP, real auth service, granted supervise scope). Cell F's participant root hosts an UNRELATED tenant's legacy monolith beside the sign-in: a manager that still read local trust fell back to that monolith and died with the #1944 corrupt-bundle text (the live reproduction), so F asserting '✓ manager up' goes red under a restored unconditional read. Cell G's root holds the remote space's OWN split records: the real conflict of authorities, which must refuse with the combination message; dropping that refusal lets the manager start on two authority paths and G goes red. Cell H re-asserts on F's output that no trust text names auth/auth.json, so a mutant that reads the monolith without the corrupt fallback (e.g. misreads it as this space's trust) is still caught.

The thirteen manager dials and the CLI control dials moved onto dialerFor in the same change are not claimed here. Each needs a live manager or a live control plane rather than this compact rig, so this fixture records the boundary instead of registering a mutation that would SURVIVE.
